newsitem.title: SPAIN: Pique defends disclosure process in Endesa deal.
newsitem.headline: Pique defends disclosure process in Endesa deal.

text.p: Spanish Industry Minister Josep Pique on Wednesday defended the procedure followed by his ministry and electricity firm Endesa in relation to its offer to buy two regional firms.

All political parties except the ruling Popular Party (PP) have criticised the fact that Endesa only informed stock market commission CNMV of the operation the day before it publicly announced it, despite advance newspaper reports on the deal.

"You don't need to inform the CNMV of negotiations, you only inform them about price-sensitive information and this arises when there are agreements which have been approved by the company boards," Pique told parliament.
Pique said he considered that 66-percent state-owned Endesa was justified in telling the CNMV it intended to buy up to 75 percent of Fecsa and Sevillana on October 17.

The Industry Ministry announced the operation on October 18 and the Spanish cabinet ratified it later in the day, although financial daily Expansion published advance details of the deal on October 10.
Pique said the information had been leaked by "groups who had an interest in the operation not going through", repeating comments which an Industry Ministry spokesman made to Reuters last week.

Asked about the possibility of speculative bourse trading based on privileged information leaked in advance of the deal, Pique said he awaited with interest an investigation by the CNMV on this subject.
